EN: <Cheering>

Speaker: Christine
EN: {Quiet, Ulysses has just entered}...didn't think you'd make it back.

Speaker: Christine
ActorNotes: [Dismissive, matter-of-fact] AUDIO: In this log, Christine is greeting Ulysses when he's come back from a difficult journey. She's still recovering on her bunk.
EN: {Dismissive, matter-of-fact}Almost didn't. Got my answers. {Rueful}Your Elijah, he met the Gods in this place, did a good job of making them question the way of things.

Speaker: Christine
EN: {Hunting instinct}Do you know where he went?

Speaker: Christine
EN: He's gone to the Sierra Madre. That's a special kind of hell. He won't come back. Someone smarter, tougher's going to kill him. If the Madre doesn't.

Speaker: Christine
EN: {Determined, angry, hates this guy}I have to go after him.

Speaker: Christine
EN: Not going to talk you out of it. Know what it means to track someone you share history with. Got a meeting of my own.

Speaker: Christine
EN: {Quiet}That Courier?

Speaker: Christine
EN: {Nods}Get her to come to me. {Beat, slow}Got a message for her, like the message she had for me.

Speaker: Christine
EN: {Cold, staring into future, slight bitterness}Make them walk the road west, straight and true, sink their feet in Old World ash. Let storms tear at them. See the Divide. See what happened.

Speaker: Christine
EN: {Divide = Dangerous, desolate area, quiet}The Divide? There's nothing there.

Speaker: Christine
EN: {Slight smile}Nothing there? Like the Big Empty? The Sierra Madre? No, the Old World sleeps there, sure as the flag I carry. The Courier knows the way.

Speaker: Christine
EN: {Closing note, foreshadowing final conflict}And at the Divide, her and I - there, we'll have an ending to things.

Speaker: Christine
ActorNotes: [Shrugs] AUDIO: In this log, Christine is debating with Ulysses, her "doctor." She's still recovering on her bunk - a little tired, but still strong.
EN: {Shrugs}No denying that. Proof's here in this crater, all around us. {Beat, slightly appraising}Your tribe, the Brotherhood - haven't met many of you. Wanted to.

Speaker: Christine
EN: {More reflective}Thought you might be the last chance for the Mojave... the West. The East. But you're all the same mind, obsessed.

Speaker: Christine
EN: {emph, correcting}Elijah is obsessed. He's mad. It's why they ordered his execution.

Speaker: Christine
EN: {"You..."}Two are more alike than you know, too wrapped in the wrong bits of history to see ahead. {Shrugs}Not judging. I know how it is.

Speaker: Christine
EN: {Quieter, reflective}People are like couriers, you and him. Sometimes don't even know the message they bring.

Speaker: Christine
EN: {Turns attention back to her}You all had a {emph}new flag. Thought maybe new ideas along with it. {Beat, quieter}What you believe isn't any better than the Bear or Bull. No future in either.

Speaker: Christine
EN: {Defiance}So says the man with the Old World flag on his back. America, the Commonwealth... burned away.

Speaker: Christine
EN: {Slight anger, low}America {emph}sleeps. And until it's dead, I carry it. Just like I carried you. More than hope. Belief.

Speaker: Christine
EN: There's voices here in the Big Empty, I want to talk to them. Not like your Elijah did. {End on a downnote, like a movie trailer going away}Got questions. Want to hear history give its answer.

Speaker: Christine
ActorNotes: [Quiet, she's in a cell - she's been tortured, but recovering]

Speaker: Christine
ActorNotes: AUDIO: In this log, Christine has just been operated on. She's not horribly weak, but definitely tired and worn out - she's committed to die.
EN: Not going to make it through this, hope someone finds this message, gets it to the Brotherhood in the West.

Speaker: Christine
EN: Tracked a rogue Brotherhood Elder, Elijah, here, to the Big Empty. {Breath}Place is more than it seems, there's a crater hidden deep inside.

Speaker: Christine
EN: Junkyard of Pre-War labs scattered across the crater's surface, all still running... {to herself, mutters}like this one.

Speaker: Christine
EN: Elijah's dissecting these centers, one by one... tracked him to an old Chinese-American internment camp. Survivors, Ghouls, have bomb collars.

Speaker: Christine
EN: Robots moved in when I tried to intercept him... Elijah sent the camp Ghouls against us both, like walking bombs.

Speaker: Christine
EN: Got hit by the explosions, woke up here. {To herself}Guess the medical robots were programmed to bring wounded victims from the camp to this center.

Speaker: Christine
EN: Some kind of Auto-Doc prototype lab... manned by corpses trapped inside suits that keep them moving, no idea why.

Speaker: Christine
EN: Not sure how long I'm going to last... cut open my head like a lot of the humans I've seen here, feel strange, can talk, but can't hack the term...{"terminal," trails off}

Speaker: Christine

Speaker: Doctor Mobius

Speaker: Doctor Mobius
EN: Your brain is here, safe with me. {Smiles}We chat over Mentats.

Speaker: Doctor Mobius
EN: {Frowns}I'm not sure except that I'm sure there's a {emph}very good raisin for it. I have very good raisins for almost everything I do.

Speaker: Doctor Mobius

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: Oh come on, that stuff's fun!
EN: {Rising emphasis with each word}Fun? Fun?! Is tetanus fun? Hmm? Is rickets? What about {SEP-sis}sepsis, enjoy that do we?

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: Oh come on, that stuff's fun!
EN: The things you do with our body are suicidally dangerous, and if you could silence your glandular impulses, you would hear me screaming at you!

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: Of course you're responsible! You're my brain!
EN: {Outrage}I most certainly am not! I am the seat of all reason and logic in our little partnership!

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: Of course you're responsible! You're my brain!
EN: All those... {vague disgust}feelings that motivate you, that sense of righteousness and that rush you get when you help someone, do you know where those come from?

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: Of course you're responsible! You're my brain!
EN: All those... {vague disgust}ugh... feelings that motivate you, those urges to hurt people, to take and crush and maim, do you know where they come from?

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: Of course you're responsible! You're my brain!
EN: All those... {vague disgust}ugh... feelings that motivate you, do you know where those come from?

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: Of course you're responsible! You're my brain!
EN: Glands. They come from glands. Free of the tyranny of your ape-like and primitive endocrine system, I can see how foolish your motives are.

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: This is too weird. I'll be back later.
EN: Barring the unlikely event that I evolve some sort of rocket-propelled locomotion, I will be here.

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: Cool! I can talk to my own brain! Can my heart and spine talk, too?
EN: {Taken aback by the player's statement}Err... yes, well, you do know that those particular organs don't have neurons and are thus incapable of speech, yes?

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: How the hell did Mobius get hold of my brain?
EN: After the Think Tank extracted me from your skull, they fell to bickering amongst themselves. I'm sad to say we were quite forgotten about.

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: How the hell did Mobius get hold of my brain?
EN: Dr. Mobius saw an opportunity to gain some leverage, and had me spirited away to his dome.

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: Why does my brain sound so... masculine?
EN: Ah, well, as to that... you'd be surprised how hard a feminine-sounding voice modulator is to find in the Forbidden Zone.

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: Why does my brain sound so... masculine?
EN: It's not as though brain-sustaining life support tanks grow on trees. I had to take what I could get.

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: Come on, let's go. We're getting out of here.
EN: Ew! Crawl back in there? Are you mad? I don't know where you've been!

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: Come on, let's go. We're getting out of here.
EN: For all I know, you're riddled with disease, or packing one of those delightful head wounds you seem to attract!

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: Come on, let's go. We're getting out of here.
EN: I'm not crawling back into your head just to ooze right back out again!

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: Come on, let's go. We're getting out of here.
EN: Well... I suppose you've convinced me well enough. I'll rejoin your body if that's your final decision.

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: Come on, let's go. We're getting out of here.
EN: Unfortunately, before we get to that stage of the proceedings, we have a problem.

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: Come on, let's go. We're getting out of here.
EN: Even if I could settle myself back in your skull and reconnect all those pesky nerve endings, Dr. Mobius doesn't have the tools here.

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: Come on, let's go. We're getting out of here.
EN: We would have to make use of Dr. Klein's lab, and I rather doubt the brains are inclined to share.

Speaker: Player / Courier
Topic_Name: Come on, let's go. We're getting out of here.
EN: So... what do you say, brain? Join me for some more wild adventures?

Speaker: Brain Tank
ActorNotes: [Beat, stunned that the player would actually say this]
Topic_Name: Actually, yes. I would love a cookie.
EN: {Beat, stunned that the player would actually say this}I... {sigh}ugh... is this really what I have to look forward to?

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: Listen, you're my brain, so you'd better be more respectful!
EN: {Sarcastic}Oh, had I? What exactly will you do if I don't? {emph}Not put me back in that cranial {dungeon}donjon you call your head? Heavens forbid!

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: Why are you such a dick?
EN: Well, that's a fine how-do-you-do! Me! A, quote, dick, unquote. As if I'm the one responsible for the way you carry on, gadding about the Wastes.

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: Why are you such a dick?
EN: I'm not the one that makes us clamber around tetanus-infested ancient Vaults or go charging off to New Vegas on missions of ill-conceived revenge!

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: Why are you such a dick?
EN: And have we forgotten who got us shot in the head and buried in a shallow grave? Hmm? Do you think I enjoyed that little moment?

Speaker: Brain Tank
EN: Ah, lovely, figured that out, have we? {slightly baby-talking, praising a small and stupid child}Would you like a cookie?

Speaker: Doctor Borous
EN: -Gabe, down! Down, boy! Stop it!-{2D}

Speaker: Doctor Borous
EN: -{Warning to dog}Now... let the intruder have the Sonic Emitter schematics. Klein wants it, all right, boy? Let the intruder dig it up wherever you buried it.-{2D}

Speaker: Doctor Borous
EN: -Gaaabe! I am sorry I put your brain in a bowl, boy. Oohhh, who's a good boy. YOU are!-{2D}

Speaker: Doctor Borous
EN: -Gabe would bark and snarl and bite whenever ANYONE came to visit.-{2D}

Speaker: Doctor Borous
EN: -That's why I replaced his legs with spare parts and fed him a steady diet of Psycho-laced dog chow.-{2D}

Speaker: Doctor Borous
EN: -Ohhhhh yes, my PET, Gabe. {Chuckles}I'd forgotten about the old boy and the COUNTLESS experiments I'd done on him back at Higgs.-{2D}

Speaker: Doctor Borous
EN: -{Eager}Gaaabe? Gabe, you're about to have your FAVORITE treat - a VISITOR. Won't that be nice? DON'T eat the visitor, boy. {Quieter}Don't. Please.-{2D}

Speaker: Doctor Borous
EN: -{Thinking}The Residential Test. Wasn't that shut down for some reason?-{2D}

Speaker: Doctor Borous

Speaker: Doctor Borous

Speaker: Doctor Borous
EN: -{Strangely matter-of-fact about this}Oh, and the tarantula hawk. Can't splice enough, I always say, especially if you can make a magnificent Cazador!-{2D}

Speaker: Doctor Borous

Speaker: Doctor Borous
EN: -This is a MOST serious matter requiring the MOST serious of detentions.-{2D}

Speaker: Doctor Borous

Speaker: Doctor Borous

Speaker: Doctor Borous

Speaker: Doctor Borous

Speaker: Doctor Borous

Speaker: Doctor Borous

Speaker: Doctor Borous

Speaker: Doctor Borous

Speaker: Doctor Borous
EN: -You are in the LIBRARY. Be quiet here and filled with SHHHHH.-{2D}

EN: Ooh, you found my mood lighting! Installing upgrade!

Speaker: Brain Tank

EN: I'm quite sure whatever he did was highly scientific, though.

Speaker: Brain Tank

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: You talk a lot of science, brain, but you don't make a lot of sense.
EN: Does that explain the matter?

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: Well, you don't have a mouth, but you can talk. Explain that, smarty-pants!

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: Well, you don't have a mouth, but you can talk. Explain that, smarty-pants!
EN: Your heart can't be wired up to a... a thought-synthesizing processor! You can't talk to it!

Speaker: Brain Tank

EN: I've been bettering myself, I'll have you know. I've been reading - actual literature, mind you, not that ¡La Fantoma! or Tæles of Chivalrie drivel.

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: Uh, brain? You seem... awful smart all of a sudden.
EN: I've been studying the classics, acquiring a solid grounding in medicine and the sciences.

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: Uh, brain? You seem... awful smart all of a sudden.
EN: Also, I'm fairly certain this tank has been liberally salted with ground Mentats.

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: All this smart-talk is hurting my head. Please stop it.
EN: Well, we certainly wouldn't want to strain your comprehension, would we?

Speaker: Brain Tank
EN: {Anguished noise of frustration}Argh!

Speaker: Brain Tank
EN: [SUCCEEDED] I... well... look, it's all a very complex system of biofeedback and other things I wouldn't expect you to understand.

Speaker: Player / Courier
EN: But you're the source of most of those glands. Unless you're arguing that my thyroid is to blame.

Speaker: Brain Tank
EN: [FAILED] And you're an expert on your own glandular delusions, are you? No, leave this one to an impartial authority: me.

Speaker: Player / Courier
EN: That doesn't seem quite right...

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: Admit it. You're just as glandular as I am.
EN: Oh, all right... perhaps I am, but at least I'm logical about it.

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: What's so bad about letting the brains get out? They don't seem that terrible.
EN: Don't seem so bad? They vivisected us just to see what would happen! Have you forgotten the Lobotomites? The Cyberdogs, I assume you saw those?

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: What's so bad about letting the brains get out? They don't seem that terrible.
EN: Imagine that kind of "science" spread across the entire Mojave. Every man, woman and child we've met reduced to a Lobotomite.

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: What's so bad about letting the brains get out? They don't seem that terrible.
EN: Is that what you want?

Speaker: Brain Tank
EN: [SUCCEEDED] {Sigh, realizes the player is right.}Well, I suppose I do miss those endorphin rushes when we save the day. All right - what's the plan?

Speaker: Player / Courier
EN: You're part of me. I know you don't want to let that happen any more than I do.

Speaker: Brain Tank
EN: [FAILED] We have to do no such thing! Just don't bring them the tools they need to get out!

Speaker: Player / Courier
EN: Come on! We have to stop them! And stuff!

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: That's going to be a problem. Until they fix me, I can't leave Big Mountain either.
EN: Hmm, I had overlooked that particular angle. Still, it's not so bad staying here, is it? We could be comfortable.

Speaker: Brain Tank

Speaker: Brain Tank

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: Come on, you're my brain and I'm your body. This is meant to be, baby!
EN: {Shaking off the horror}Anyways, even if... {disgust}that... was on the table, we have a problem.

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: Too bad. I've got arms, you don't. You're coming with me.
EN: I can see there's going to be no reasoning with you at all, is there? I'm nothing more than a slave to your deranged, glandular whims.

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: I can see your point. What can I do to make this a fair compromise?
EN: If you want me back, we need to establish some ground rules.

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: I can see your point. What can I do to make this a fair compromise?
EN: First, showers! Second, regular check-ups. {emph}Regular, mind you, and from a reputable doctor.

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: I can see your point. What can I do to make this a fair compromise?
EN: That Julie Farkas woman, for example. She seems to know a thing or two.

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: I can see your point. What can I do to make this a fair compromise?
EN: Third, you need to listen to me more than your hormonal choir and genitalian orchestra. Promise me that, and you've got a deal.

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: But what about the good things? What about crushing those who oppose you, the smell of fire... loot?
EN: All motivated by nothing but an imbalance in certain brain chemicals. The tank corrects for that - I feel no urge toward antisocial behavior.

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: But what about the good things? What about a cool breeze on your cheek, the smell of food... love?
EN: Overrated biological feedback. Believe me, you only feel that way because you've got all that meat... oozing hormones.

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: Don't you want to be reunited? I thought you'd be happy to get back into my head!
EN: I'm not going to lie to you, the prospect is definitely not that appealing.

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: Don't you want to be reunited? I thought you'd be happy to get back into my head!
EN: Look at it from my perspective. Here, I have peace, quiet, and safety - well, barring the odd rogue scorpion.

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: Don't you want to be reunited? I thought you'd be happy to get back into my head!
EN: In your head, I've got poison, radiation, grisly injuries, and biological functions.

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: Don't you want to be reunited? I thought you'd be happy to get back into my head!
EN: Do you know how much more you can get done when you're not constantly looking for places to urinate? It's quite a lot, I can tell you.

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: What about you? That tank isn't exactly looking springtime fresh.
EN: {Taken aback, player has caught him}I... well... that's a completely different matter! The tank isn't biological, it's not the same at all!

Speaker: Brain Tank
EN: {sarcastic, maybe a little baby-talk}Oh yes, I rather expect you have. You must have been swamped, you poor dear. Why don't you relax and put your feet up?

Speaker: Brain Tank
EN: I've just been traumatically scooped out of my body and plugged into this jar, that's all. But, you've been {emph}busy.

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: Yes. Because running around a crater full of bizarre science experiments, hygiene is a top priority.
EN: Well, I see sarcasm hasn't eluded you. Fine, perhaps now isn't the best time, but it's the principle of the thing.

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: There's no need to be sarcastic. Meeting your own brain is a slightly odd event.
EN: Yes, well, believe me, the opposite is equally true. Good Lord, have you bathed at all since they pulled me out of you?

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: Let's just say violence is the last resort of the civilized man, and I'm feeling mighty uncivilized.
EN: With an attitude like that, it's small wonder you got yourself shot in the head.

Speaker: Brain Tank
EN: [SUCCEEDED] Not much of one for the high-tech approach, are we? Well, I suppose we'd best get on with it.

Speaker: Player / Courier

Speaker: Brain Tank
EN: [FAILED] Hmm... yes, I don't think you've {emph}quite thought this through yet.

Speaker: Brain Tank
EN: [SUCCEEDED] Going the old-fashioned route, are we? I rather like it. What's next?

EN: The brains have forgotten the little things. Things like sharp blades and heavy chunks of steel.

Speaker: Brain Tank
EN: [FAILED] Before you go that route, do me a favor and read up on the history of battles in which men with swords fought giant brains with lasers.

Speaker: Player / Courier
EN: I thought since they like lasers so much, I'd surprise them. With a club or something.

Speaker: Brain Tank
EN: [SUCCEEDED] Well, you have always been thorough in your destruction. All right, what's your plan?

Speaker: Player / Courier
EN: Ever had a squirrel brain omelet? That, but on a bigger scale. And with bombs.

Speaker: Brain Tank
EN: [FAILED] I see. And you plan to be standing in the midst of this mayhem? Well, that's a novel strategy.

Speaker: Player / Courier
EN: I think bombs? Yeah, maybe bombs.

Speaker: Brain Tank
EN: [SUCCEEDED] Oh, energy weapons. Yes... I'd almost forgotten how much fun those are. How do we proceed, then?

Speaker: Player / Courier
EN: I'm going to show them what's really the brightest thing in the room.

Speaker: Brain Tank
EN: [FAILED] I hate to say it, but your ability to handle high-tech energy weapons doesn't exactly instill within me great confidence.

Speaker: Player / Courier
EN: We've got lasers, right? I thought we'd use lasers.

Speaker: Brain Tank
EN: [SUCCEEDED] Hmm... now that you mention it, I do miss that lovely "rat-a-tat boom" a bit. It's just not the same without a body to feel the recoil.

Speaker: Brain Tank
EN: What's the next step, then?

Speaker: Player / Courier
EN: I'm going to give them a demonstration of the physics behind small, fast-moving chunks of lead.

Speaker: Brain Tank
EN: [FAILED] Yes, I think you haven't quite got the hang of punning yet.

Speaker: Player / Courier
EN: I'm going to introduce them to a world of pain. Bullet pain.

Speaker: Brain Tank

Speaker: Brain Tank
Topic_Name: Are you really saying you'd let the Think Tank outwit us?

Speaker: Robobrain

EN: {Innocent wonder}What is this strange new world around me? What does it hold in store for a dreamer such as myself?

Speaker: Robobrain

Speaker: Robobrain
EN: {Innocent voice, waking up}Who... am I? I... feel different, awake, alive for the first time ever.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: I'm not planning to go into the Divide after you.
EN: No Courier would go to the Divide... but you will. And that's what sets us apart - we walk roads no other Courier will walk.{No sound file}

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: I'm not planning to go into the Divide after you.
EN: And for you... you'll want to see your home one last time, see what happened.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: I'm not planning to go into the Divide after you.
EN: You're curious. You walk, leave ruin in your path... you can't leave alone. Still, the choice is yours... what I offer, it's the last I offer you.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: I'm not planning to go into the Divide after you.
EN: I don't care if you walk the Divide. Turn, walk the Mojave, fight beneath the flags... but you'll wonder.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: I'm not planning to go into the Divide after you.
EN: If you don't, the Divide will come to you, and the Mojave. That will be my message to you, like the message you had for me.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: The Long 15 is no more. The main supply line into NCR is cut.
EN: No damage done, not yet. Maybe in years. Keeps the Bear fenced... if Caesar can't drive it back, fire might.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: The Long 15 is no more. The main supply line into NCR is cut.
EN: Only delays the end for the Bull, a new wall for them to scale and cross... once they're done with the Mojave. And Hoover Dam.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: The Long 15 is no more. The main supply line into NCR is cut.
EN: Never again do you or any other courier and caravan need walk that route. Let the Mojave breathe without that asphalt scar raking it.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: Dry Wells is destroyed - that was your birthplace?
EN: No, opposite of that. It's where my tribe was taken. Where another history was put to the blade, lesson taught.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: Dry Wells is destroyed - that was your birthplace?
EN: It is where we realized Vulpes did not approach us as equals. Where we realized the wolf had come, and we watched our history die.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: Dry Wells is destroyed - that was your birthplace?
EN: Now it belongs to Legion... and all the death there now belongs to them as well. Not revenge... just the way of things when you {emph}own them.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: I wanted to hear more about Hoover Dam.
EN: Old World wall, run red with blood of Bear and Bull. It'll bleed more before the sun sets on the Mojave.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: I wanted to hear more about Hoover Dam.
EN: That place and I have a past, owe it a debt - and it owes me. If your path takes you there, know you're not the only one.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: I wanted to hear more about Hoover Dam.
EN: It's the wall by which this age will be measured, the gravestone of the Mojave. Old World never meant it as such.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: A question one could have asked you not long ago, before walking the road West into the storms.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: Need to be here, see what was done. It's custom of the Bear to never see the marks it claws in the land... not {emph}my custom.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: Maybe that's why you've come, too - need to see where the missile from Ashton touched ground down below, in Hopeville... the Courier's Mile.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: Need to be here, see what was done. In the Divide, in Hopeville... the Courier's Mile.

Speaker: Player / Courier
EN: Can you tell me again what you're doing here?

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: Was hoping you could help me shape something.
EN: {Nods}Let's see what gifts the Mojave has for us.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: Was hoping you could help me shape something.
EN: {Looking at player's inventory}Let's make something new from the old.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: What did you mean, "slower death for the Mojave?"
EN: [SUCCEEDED] {Nod}Death'll come from below. {Frowns}In the Divide, need to watch the sky {emph}and ground... {Dismissive, shakes head}Mojave'll be easy prey for them.

Speaker: Player / Courier
Topic_Name: What did you mean, "slower death for the Mojave?"
EN: When you say, "slower death for the Mojave," you mean they're spreading out from the Divide.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: What did you mean, "slower death for the Mojave?"
EN: [FAILED] Mojave needs to survive itself first... does that, Tunnelers will be next on the list.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: If this is the High Road... where does it lead?
EN: At the end of the High Road lies Ashton - its silo.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: If this is the High Road... where does it lead?
EN: {Disgust, hates ED-E}That {emph}machine with you, it can open it, wake it up, {quieter}like it did the one in Hopeville.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: Some of the flayed Hopeville soldiers looked like NCR... but fought beside others in Legion armor.
EN: {Quieter}You see true. Not scavengers... it's what they wore {slight beat}before this all happened.{No sound file}

Speaker: Player / Courier
Topic_Name: Some of the flayed Hopeville soldiers looked like NCR... but fought beside others in Legion armor.
EN: [NCR] Those soldiers in Hopeville... were once NCR, I'm sure of it. Why were they with the Legion?

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: Some of the flayed Hopeville soldiers looked like NCR... but fought beside others in Legion armor.
EN: Pain makes for strange allies... the hate the Bear and Bull shared across the battlefield, now turned against the Divide. Few survived... intact.{No sound file}

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: Some of the flayed Hopeville soldiers looked like NCR... but fought beside others in Legion armor.
EN: Many NCR were already here when the destruction happened. Keeping the route East open, in fear of Caesar. Fear of the Legion.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: Those Marked Men in Hopeville - some had strange masks and blades I'd never seen before.
EN: {Quieter}You haven't seen enough of the Legion yet to see what they worship... what they hold on to, even after what happened to them.{No sound file}

Speaker: Player / Courier
Topic_Name: Those Marked Men in Hopeville - some had strange masks and blades I'd never seen before.
EN: [Legion] Those Legionnaires in Hopeville wore Legion armor - and strange masks and blades.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: Those Marked Men in Hopeville - some had strange masks and blades I'd never seen before.
EN: They bear false versions of Legate Lanius' mask, the one Caesar fashioned for him. Thought it was an insult at first.... {to himself}know better now.{No sound file}

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: Those Marked Men in Hopeville - some had strange masks and blades I'd never seen before.
EN: It's shaped from Divide metal, not with care and strength, but with hate. Keeps them anchored.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: Those Marked Men in Hopeville - some had strange masks and blades I'd never seen before.
EN: Crude, effective - like the blades they carry, distant mirrors of their Legate. A symbol they can hold on to - while the Divide tears at them.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: What were the creatures in the underpass?
EN: Tunnelers. Predators that make their own roads beneath the ground here.{No sound file}

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: What were the creatures in the underpass?
EN: {Somber}Divide broke their sky, showed them the world above - and the scent of new prey.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: What were the creatures in the underpass?
EN: Be a slower death for the Mojave than bombs and fire... but they'll come for its people, from where they least expect - below.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: You delivered a package. Had markings that matched those in the Divide. Not all... but enough.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: Military markings, from some place the Bear had savaged in the West. {Beat, trying to draw player out here}Maybe seeing those markings on it reminded you of home... made you carry it.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: This canyon is miles long - maybe longer. Where can I find you?
EN: At the end of the Divide, through the trenches and wreckage - that's where you'll find me. My new home, here, amongst dead men.{No sound file}

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: This canyon is miles long - maybe longer. Where can I find you?
EN: You and that {slight sneer at 'machine'}machine, keep your eyes on the tower that cuts the horizon... you'll find your way. Made it this far... not much farther to go.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: ...back again. Left that crater behind. Got a few holotapes left, ones from the medical center.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: The woman... she fixed the recorder. Said it wouldn't last, repayment for me fixing her. She doesn't like debts, can respect that.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: Payment enough, just to hear someone who believes in the Brotherhood of Steel. Not Elijah. Different view. Same madness.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: She answered me on their philosophy, their way of seeing - the roads they walk. {Disgust}Dead-ends. Empty... as if technology can solve anything.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: {Quiet, reflective}Big Empty's proof where that road leads. {Beat}Just like the Divide, and all the roads that lead to it.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: I walked the Great Salt Lake as Caesar's eye, then his hand.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: Mongrels there, two-legs and four. Saw the walls of New Canaan the scavengers circled... hadn't the strength or fire to take. Too high, too strong.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: White Legs, they were born for war, they run to it, hungry for battle... yet their hunger is to be a part of history, something larger.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: Like the Legion. As always, brought them a message - from Caesar.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: {Paraphrasing message from Caesar}If New Canaan burns, Caesar might {emph}see them. {Scoffs}"Might." Even the chance was a lie.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: To honor Caesar - destroy the {emph}history of New Canaan, and the way they {emph}carry it - in their generations and family.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: Caesar respects such strength, I told them. That - that was truth, even if "strength" wasn't the word. {Correcting}Obedience.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: You must be willing to kill {emph}anyone, children, mothers, the weak, elders... if these New Canaanites value the generations, that is what you must kill.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: It was like Vulpes was speaking through me. Use the night, silence, and fire to change their words to pleas, to screams.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: No need for bombs when hate will do.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: I... asked the White Legs to destroy a people with ancestry, going back thousands of years - another death of history, lost to time.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: The New Canaanites... they supplied medicine. Food, traded with others. Civilization, a hand from the past, not history...

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: ...but maybe a past deeper, farther than that to a place where this... {beat}God really exists.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: {Dismissive}If so, his handiwork and people belong elsewhere, not in this place. Another symbol, like Bear and Bull, with no meaning in the present.

Speaker: Ulysses
ActorNotes: [Studying weather, log to himself, thinking back]
EN: {Studying weather, log to himself, thinking back}Emptiness here - like the sands of the Great Salt Lake, echoed. {Beat}The beating in the Divide sky... like storm drums of the White Legs.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: {Introspective}Ran with them on the salt beds, at Caesar's command - {recalling Caesar's orders, echoing them}cut the throats of the two-headed Bear, cut all communities off.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: Use storm, sky. Disease. Fire, starvation... and the violence of the ignorant to ruin all who {emph}could... might stand against him.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: But the White Legs... they couldn't live on their own, like most scavengers. So gave them purpose - turned their hunger into a weapon.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: The wall of New {CANE-in}Canaan... too high for Caesar. Too proud, maybe - {quiet}or maybe something there, from his past, that needed killing. Memory of Graham.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: Helped them dig out Canaan supply caches, and other secrets the sands hid - bunkers, filled with powered weapons even the Brotherhood might desire.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: They called these new weapons "storm drums" in the firing of shells. Taught them the power in the casings... to channel the spirits in their guns.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: Me... they called me the Flag-Bearer. Glory in my hand, in my staff that still bore the weight of the Old World just as the symbol on my back did.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: I learned their weapons as a means of respect. And when it came their turn to pay respect to me... history came rushing back.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: {Quiet, bring to a close}Can't escape what's been done. History's there... no matter how far you walk.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: Have you ever wanted to speak to history - just to know the why of it? {Beat}I don't. Not any longer.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: There's old stories about gods and men, past history, into myth - where the gods, they're like children... petulant, cruel.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: {Emph}Those were the voices of the Big Empty, the past. Couldn't leave well enough alone, had to ask. Had to ask the why of it.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: {Slight frustration}Their answers were madness. And power, stronger than me, would take a hundred Elijahs... someone tougher than him or I to best them in their Dome.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: They didn't know why they were there, what had led to that point, their names - like serpents devouring themselves, cannibalizing their own thoughts.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: When all seemed lost, thought it was the end - my anger gave me strength to ask them my last question.

Speaker: Ulysses
ActorNotes: [Echoing the question he asked the Think Tank]
EN: {Echoing the question he asked the Think Tank}"Who are you, that do not know your history?"

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: {Slight reverence}And they awoke. For... a short time.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: The flag you wear, they said. We remember. America.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: It wasn't just a flag to them... it was a place, an idea they had {emph}cared for. Once.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: They told me what it was like to grow in that world... all they had done to lift it up... protect it. They... didn't know it was gone, that...

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: ...yet they had cared once. Before forgetting their history.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: As they were talking... kept seeing the Courier's shadow behind them, giving each their words weight. History cast aside... a home, left behind.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: I listened. I asked. Was there anything left? {Emph}Anything that still carries America's voice?

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: And they told me I had already been there. I and one other, walking right out of history deeper than we knew.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: They told me what lies in the heart of the Divide, what can be found there. And the words to awaken it - and the one to speak them.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: Big Empty - there's something hidden there, a crater, past wind and sand - so deep in the desert, there's no turning back.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: Finding the crater was an accident, was following the weather patterns - the Divide sky torn like that, man's violence, not nature's.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: That violence in the sky, had a source. Tracked it. Like following a river current.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: Left the colors to mark my way, like always, case someone finds them, learns the pattern - the Courier might.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: When I thought sand and wind would never end... came to the crater.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: And there... there was an Old World facility, a weather station, at the edge, still raking the sky with electricity and generators.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: And beyond it... saw the rest of the Old World hell there, all carved up like garden plots. Had to see what was there, couldn't leave it be.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: {Slight irritation}Things sleep in the Big Empty, the Brotherhood woke them up - can't move quiet, any more than the two-headed Bear can.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: And when they woke up, it was like all of history waking up at once. Almost didn't make it out. {Beat, quiet}Almost. Left with answers I never intended.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: Last tape, last message. In case... you best me. If you're hearing this, you have, through blood or word.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: This message, and all that lies with it - it is for you, Courier. If you want to know the... why of things.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: This world, I've walked a good part of it... I stopped only because of you. What you did - gave me pause.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: Long ago, I crossed the Colorado, the first among the Legion to see Hoover Dam in all its glory... an Old World wall, yet bridging two sides.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: {Quieter}And beyond it, a symbol of a two-headed Bear, an idea great enough to challenge Caesar himself.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: Might kill him, taking it, whether he won or lost. The Bull needs to fight, needs the challenge, without it... it falters, dies in the dust.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: {To himself}Might be a lesson there, in you and me. {"I'll"}Leave the thought behind the message to you.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: My message is this - the destruction that has been wrought, at the Divide - or elsewhere, if you couldn't stop me...

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: It can happen again. It will {emph}keep happening.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: If war doesn't change, men must change, and so must their symbols. {Beat, quiet}Even if it is nothing at all, know what you follow, Courier...

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: ...just as I followed you, to the end. Whatever your symbol...

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: ...carry it on your back, and wear it proudly when you stand at Hoover Dam.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: The White Legs... meant to show respect, bribe me for Caesar's favor, echoing mannerisms and words...

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: Showed them tech caches, taught them the workings of chamber and powder, spoke of Caesar's {emph}pride in those that used such things... lies. And...

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: {quiet disgust}...and then... they tried to honor {emph}me - not the Legion.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: They brought me before the campfire one night, showed me how they changed themselves, how they wore their hair now.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: It was like my entire dead tribe in the firelight, teeth grinning red in the dark - eager corpses, blood-covered ghosts.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: They... had taken my braids, the way of the Twisted Hairs, as if it showed they were {emph}like me, {emph}of me...

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: ...while every knot in their braids spoke of raping, violence - and ignorance of what the knots {emph}meant. They thought to show respect... defiled it.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: Lost myself in trying to read the braids they wove, when I remembered they had put no meaning in it. They had no history of what it meant.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: They didn't even know the insult in the twists, knots... and Dry Wells came rushing back, the White Legs circled like that...

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: It was like looking at the dead of my tribe, reborn as ghosts - hateful, hungry, bowing to Caesar. {Quiet, bring to a close}Another history... gone, carried by me alone.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: Find anything in the dust of Hopeville?
EN: Nothing but wind, sand... ash. More may reveal itself in time, not now.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: Find anything in the dust of Hopeville?
EN: If you're determined, return, might be something new surfaces.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: Find anything in the dust of Hopeville?
EN: Wind and blood has uncovered more beneath the soil.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: Find anything in the dust of Hopeville?
EN: If you want these Old World relics, they're yours... better you carry them than the Marked Men.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: Is this where you're making camp?
EN: Not a camp - vigil, maybe. Never claimed it as mine. {More a question}If anyone owns the Divide... {"well..."}your claim is stronger than mine.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: Is this where you're making camp?
EN: Don't feel like adding a campfire to the ones that already burn below. {Beat, making offer}If you brought Mojave gifts, might be able to shape something for the road.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: Is this where you're making camp?
EN: Depends what history has to say about them. There's a lot the land can provide... if you know the road that led to it.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: Is this where you're making camp?
EN: Mojave's got ways of healing most ills - if not, some tribe's usually found a way you didn't expect.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: Is this where you're making camp?
EN: Like Healing Powders. Tribes back West only use Xander and Broc flower. There's a way the Twin Mothers in the East used to brew it, though.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: Is this where you're making camp?
EN: Called it Bitter Drink, mixed up the Xander and Broc in a bottle, added some kick to it so your head doesn't get all clouded.

Speaker: Player / Courier
Topic_Name: Is this where you're making camp?
EN: Any recipes you can teach?

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: Is this where you're making camp?
EN: {Thinking}Antivenom's helpful around the Mojave with the Bark Scorpions. Even one sting can kill you. {Beat}Tunneler bite can be just as bad.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: Is this where you're making camp?
EN: My tribe, Twisted Hairs, had a better way than Antivenom, if you act fast.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: Is this where you're making camp?
EN: Snakebite Tourniquet - cuts off the venom, no need to scavenge glands and blood. {Himself, slight disgust}Or drink that mess.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: Is this where you're making camp?
EN: Part of the reason we wore our hair like we did, {corrects self}like I do now.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: Is this where you're making camp?
EN: Here's some for the road - trick to making it's not hard. {Beat}Get bit, hook and twist it. Fast as blinking, doesn't give poison time to sink in.

Speaker: Player / Courier
Topic_Name: Is this where you're making camp?
EN: Any more recipes.. or histories... you can teach?

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: Is this where you're making camp?
EN: Nothing more than I've already shared. We'll have to keep with what we know. {Beat}Tired of history's lessons, anyway.

Speaker: Player / Courier
Topic_Name: Is this where you're making camp?
EN: Any more recipes you can teach?

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: {Matter-of-fact}Questions have a habit of making others.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: The Divide's irradiated... are you sure you want to stay here?
EN: The invisible fires burn here, true enough. Still... to have helped carry out such an act, then not face it...

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: The Divide's irradiated... are you sure you want to stay here?
EN: Not my way. If my life burns out here, so be it... until then, I wait and watch, see what the road brings.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: That's part of why I'm here. Watch them - if they attack me, try to enter the Mojave, I answer. {Little quieter}Not looking to kill them... save them, if I can.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: There might be something saving in them. {Quieter, to himself}If not, then what I do is mercy, not murder.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: What's the Courier's Mile? Is that where the Ashton missile hit?
EN: My name for it. If you have a better one, you grant it - my choice in names won't carry past you and I.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: What's the Courier's Mile? Is that where the Ashton missile hit?
EN: Lies along the road, running from the Hopeville silo... straight on to where the ground burns, and wind howls even stronger than here.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: Your tapes prove you've walked the Mojave, yet learned the wrong lessons.
EN: Comes down to perspective, how far one's walked, and what they've left behind.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: Your tapes prove you've walked the Mojave, yet learned the wrong lessons.
EN: {Challenging}If you challenge this moment, let's hear your perspective. If my words are all you have, let's hear them.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: So... you think dropping bombs on the Mojave is going to solve things?
EN: [SUCCEEDED] {Thinking}The why of it... you taught me the why of it.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: So... you think dropping bombs on the Mojave is going to solve things?
EN: If you believe in something enough, you must be willing to let it burn, lest it claim you.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: So... you think dropping bombs on the Mojave is going to solve things?
EN: These governments of the two-headed bear... the Legion... they carry Old World ideas into an age that no longer needs them, where they cannot live.

Speaker: Player / Courier
Topic_Name: So... you think dropping bombs on the Mojave is going to solve things?
EN: I need to know why you're doing this - not for my sake, for history's sake.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: So... you think dropping bombs on the Mojave is going to solve things?
EN: [FAILED] Yes, that is what you proved to me at the Divide - what is here, what you showed me... it is enough.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: So... you think dropping bombs on the Mojave is going to solve things?
EN: You don't understand. {Beat}You will.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: You've wasted enough of my time. Get ready to die.
EN: {DUPE}I'll finish history's work. If the Divide couldn't kill you... perhaps these spears of the Old World can.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: You've wasted enough of my time. Get ready to die.
EN: {DUPE}Let's end this, Courier, you and I. Here, with the Old World flag as witness.

Speaker: Player / Courier
Topic_Name: You've wasted enough of my time. Get ready to die.
EN: I've heard enough. You're a Legion traitor, and now you'll die.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: Can you share the recipe with me?
EN: Can do that and one better... {looking around}just enough around to mix some. Here - might make the Twin Mothers' history live a little longer, you carrying it.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: Can you share the recipe with me?
EN: {Warning}When you drink it, down it all in one shot, or your stomach's not going to want to keep going after the second drink.

Speaker: Ulysses
ActorNotes: [Smiles, "you want to know the history of it?"]
EN: {Smiles, "you want to know the history of it?"}History? Cures a wound, leaves the bitterness that caused it. {To himself, scorn}The Twin Mothers were always about lessons.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: Caesar taught them the last one, though, so that's it for them. Recipe still exists, Legion uses it on forced marches with wounded soldiers.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: Wouldn't have made it through Crimson River Trail a few years back without it  - losing so much blood early on, was a Cazador feast.

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: Enough Xander root and Broc flower along the trail though, the Legion was able to keep pace and get where they were going.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: Have you been to Hopeville since the Ashton missile hit?
EN: {Reflective}Walk there sometimes, keep the walks short. Still... it's important to see. Something else to answer for.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: Have you been to Hopeville since the Ashton missile hit?
EN: Occasionally sift through the dust, the buildings... see if I can find some history. Marks of America.

Speaker: Ulysses
Topic_Name: Have you been to Hopeville since the Ashton missile hit?
EN: If you want them, keep them... you've earned it. Nothing to be gained by me holding them, and more will surface in time.

Speaker: ED-E
Topic_Name: You'd better level with me, trashcan, or I might stuff you back in that pod.
EN: <Apologetic beeping>{NPCRobotEdEDenied}

Speaker: ED-E

Speaker: ED-E

Speaker: ED-E

Speaker: ED-E

Speaker: ED-E

Speaker: Ulysses

Speaker: Ulysses

Speaker: Ulysses
EN: {Narration}At the end of the struggle, only one Courier remained in the heart of the Divide. The {emph}true Courier, Courier Six.

Speaker: Ulysses

Speaker: Ulysses
